summary: Feed s094_single is degraded: IDS port (1 Gbps) is severely overloaded by 3.22 Gbps bursts (322% of capacity across 3 intervals). All other checks (duplicates, encrypted share, VLANs, one-way, packet drops) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering bursty aggregate traffic peaking at 3.22 Gbps in 1ms intervals to a single 1 Gbps IDS port without load-balancing or shaping. This exceeds port capacity by 3.2x (threshold 0.8) and caused 3 overloaded intervals.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS will drop excess packets at ingress, causing missed signatures, broken TCP reassembly and incomplete payload inspection. As an IDS requiring both directions and full payload, overload creates blind spots for intrusion detection.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 3-4 IDS ports (or upgrade to 10 Gbps) with flow-aware 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port utilization below 80% while preserving both directions of each flow for detection.
